# LexiKey

> Free spelling practice through typing, organised by phonics rule rather than
> word frequency. Built for dyslexic learners and anyone who keeps misspelling
> the same words. Not a words-per-minute trainer.

LexiKey is a web app at https://lexikey.org. It is free, needs no account to
start, and has no timer, leaderboard or reward loop, deliberately, because
those work against the learners it is for. There is nothing to buy.

## How it works

- 1,114 words sorted into 108 phonics groups following the Orton-Gillingham
  approach, the method dyslexia specialists have used for eighty years. A
  session drills one spelling pattern, so learning "shine" transfers to "stripe".
  Patterns include short vowels, magic e, digraphs, blends, vowel teams,
  r-controlled vowels, diphthongs, silent letters, double letters, compound
  words, longer multisyllable words and a set of tricky rules.
- Every word is spoken aloud by a recorded voice (British or American), not a
  browser speech synthesiser. Speed is adjustable.
- Two modes: type the word shown on screen, or switch to dictation and type
  what is spoken. They are levelled and scored separately because reading and
  hearing a word are different skills.
- Hesitation is tracked, not just errors. A word typed correctly after a pause
  of more than 1.5 seconds has not been learned; it returns in later sessions
  until it is right three times running. Keystrokes are checked in the browser
  and never sent to a server; only session summaries are stored.
- A placement test finds the learner's level so practice starts at the gaps.
- Adjustable font, size and letter spacing, high contrast, dark mode.

## Who it is for

- Dyslexic students from upper primary through secondary school. The screen
  is plain (a word, a sentence, nothing else), so teenagers do not find it
  childish.
- Parents of children who keep failing the same spellings.
- Learning support and SEN teachers who need something free that runs in a
  browser with nothing to install. There is no teacher dashboard yet;
  progress lives in each student's own free account.
- Orton-Gillingham tutors, as homework between lessons.

## What it does not do

- It cannot diagnose dyslexia. That needs a qualified assessor.
- It does not teach reading, comprehension or writing. Only spelling.
- It does not teach touch typing or measure words per minute.
- It does not explain phonics rules; it drills them. It is not aligned to any
  named published Orton-Gillingham programme.
- It does not replace a human tutor, who can read a child's mood and adjust.
  It is what fills the six days between tutoring sessions.

## Pages

- https://lexikey.org/welcome: what LexiKey is and who it is for
- https://lexikey.org/typing-practice-for-dyslexic-students: for dyslexic teenagers and secondary students
- https://lexikey.org/orton-gillingham-spelling-practice: the practice half of Orton-Gillingham, online and free
- https://lexikey.org/free-dyslexia-tool-for-schools: for learning support teachers and schools
- https://lexikey.org/spelling-tutor: honest comparison with hiring a tutor
- https://lexikey.org/how-it-works: the Orton-Gillingham method behind it
- https://lexikey.org/for-parents: for parents of struggling spellers
- https://lexikey.org/for-teachers: classroom use and what it tracks
- https://lexikey.org/placement-test: find the learner's starting level
- https://lexikey.org/privacy: what is stored
- https://lexikey.org/: the practice app itself

## Who made it

Built by James Dimonaco, a dyslexic software developer, because writing a word
out ten times never made it stick and years of typing accidentally did.
